title: Pathaanon se Kehna — Ajay Devgn Just Dropped Bollywood's Most Combustible Teaser of the Year
excerpt: A Kashmir monologue, a Rajput clan name, and a Srinagar MP calling for a takedown — Chauhaan is still a year from release, and it is already on fire
body:
The teaser is barely two minutes long. It opens with a voiceover about 75 years of unresolved conflict in Kashmir, shows Ajay Devgn in the kind of brooding close-up that has been his calling card for three decades, and then lands a single line that has set social media ablaze: "Pathaanon se kehna… Chauhaan aa raha hai."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Czvourwg_30

Tell the Pathans. Chauhaan has arrived.

Within 48 hours, a Rajput cultural body has issued a formal condemnation, a Member of Parliament from Srinagar has demanded the teaser be taken down, and the internet is locked in the kind of furious, exhilarating argument that Bollywood claims it never designs but somehow always delivers.

**"The legacy of the Chauhans belongs to Rajput history, not to electoral or ideological purposes." — Kshatriya Parishad

Then came the political escalation."**

Chauhaan, directed by Neeraj Yadav and produced by Jio Studios and Aanand L Rai's Colour Yellow Productions, was announced on the birth anniversary of Ajay's late father, the legendary action director Veeru Devgan. The film is slated for a theatrical release on October 1, 2027 — which means the teaser dropped more than fifteen months before the movie hits screens. That is not marketing. That is provocation with a calendar.

The Kshatriya Parishad, a prominent Rajput socio-cultural organisation, fired the first volley. In a statement posted to X, they "strongly condemned" what they called an attempt to "appropriate the Chauhan clan name for contemporary communal politics." The objection is pointed: the Chauhans are a historic Rajput lineage, and the Parishad argues that their identity should not be weaponised for ideological narratives. They cited multiple historical alliances between Rajput and Pathan rulers — Mahmud Lodi fighting under Maharana Sanga, Hakim Khan Sur in Maharana Pratap's army — as evidence that the Rajput-Pathan binary the teaser invokes is, historically, fiction.

"Rajput history is not a political prop. The legacy of the Chauhans belongs to Rajput history, not to electoral or ideological purposes." — Kshatriya Parishad

Then came the political escalation. Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, the MP from Srinagar, called the teaser "offensive to Kashmiris" and urged its immediate removal. The Kashmir monologue in the opening frames, he argued, reduces a complex, painful history to a backdrop for action-hero theatrics.

Here is what makes this interesting: none of this is accidental. Ajay Devgn has navigated Bollywood's political currents longer than almost anyone working today. From Tanhaji to Bhuj to the Singham franchise, he has built an entire late-career identity on muscular, saffron-coded nationalism. Whether you find that thrilling or exhausting depends entirely on your politics, but what is undeniable is that it works — commercially, consistently, and spectacularly.

The "Pathaanon se kehna" line is the most calculated piece of dialogue in a Bollywood teaser this year. It invokes Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan without naming it, positions the Chauhan identity as the answer to whatever threat the Pathans represent, and does all of this with the plausible deniability of a historical reference. It is, by any measure, masterful marketing. It is also, depending on who you ask, deeply irresponsible.

Lost in the noise is the fact that this is an Aanand L Rai production — the man behind Raanjhanaa, Tanu Weds Manu, and Atrangi Re. Rai's filmography is built on tenderness, on complicated love stories that refuse easy binaries. His involvement suggests Chauhaan may have more nuance than its teaser lets on. Or it may simply mean that even Bollywood's most sensitive filmmakers understand where the money is.

Ajay, for his part, is having the busiest stretch of his career. Dhamaal 4 arrives July 10. Drishyam 3 follows in October. Golmaal 5 is in development. At 57, he is everywhere — and now, with Chauhaan, he is also the most controversial man in Indian cinema.

The film is fifteen months away. The debate has already started. Bollywood would not have it any other way.
author: Diaspora Desk
